chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about Al-Hasba, so he said:

My father used to encamp at Al-Abtah for a short time, then he would come and enter the houses without sleeping at Al-Abtah. So I said to him, 'What is your view if someone departs early during the two days, if he was from the people of Yemen, is it upon him to encamp at Al-Hasba?' He said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْيَمَنِ: The people of Yemen, referring to a specific group with distinct Hajj rituals
key_terms.الْأَبْطَحَ: Al-Abtah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims would encamp
key_terms.الْحَصْبَةِ: Al-Hasba, a specific location in Mina used for encamping during Hajj
key_terms.يَحْصُبُ: To encamp or stay at a specific place (specifically Al-Hasba)
key_terms.يَوْمَيْنِ: The two days of Tashriq (11th and 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory for people of Yemen to encamp at Al-Hasba if they leave early during the two days of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the juristic ruling on *al-Hasba* (encamping at Mina) for Yemeni pilgrims who perform *Qidam* (early arrival), establishing that their early departure exempts them from the mandatory stay. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj rituals, distinguishing between the general obligation for most pilgrims and the specific concession for those traveling from distant regions like Yemen. The narration also underscores the continuity of practice from Imam al-Baqir to Imam al-Sadiq, reinforcing the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation of ritual law.
